text: The separation-of-duty check is published as POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise/separation-of-duty on the base of Template and Rules §R4 and DP-13, with the resolved role codes, the subject reference and the time of the sign-in in, and a decision of ALLOWED or REFUSED with the conflicting pair, its conflict version and its reason out.
why: Architecture v5 slide 14 names POST /authorise (role, scope, DoA) for this service and gives it no separation-of-duty path; the Ownership Map has no api row for the check and TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A lists neither, so neither the path nor the payload is a source value and both must be fixed by the contract or the app story cannot be built on Day 1.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41 (P4 first API path /authorise); Ownership Map v1 api list; TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; RWB-AD-005 Story and Acceptance criteria
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 1, 3, 4, 7 (AC1), 8 (BR1), 11 and 12.1; RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 1, 4 and 12.1 through RWB-P4-AD005-CON
confirm: rwb-access contract owner with the sign-in contract owner at the wave 4 design gate
impact: Fixes the one operation the sign-in calls and the only view of the rule the estate has; a different path or payload is a contract change and a new major version, and it adds no table, no topic and no queue

text: A refusal is carried by one decision-record entry with decision code AC-DENY and reason code ROLE_CONFLICT, addressed to the security administrator, and MSG-P4-006 names the two role codes with its message ID fixed and no text of this run's own: no incident queue, no incident operation and no access event is invented for a refusal, and where the sibling sign-in story declares a text for the same message ID the two agree before the freeze.
why: AC1 and FSD P4 v3 require an incident to the security administrator and a refusal event, and no source names an incident queue, an incident operation, a target service or an event of this service for a refusal; MSG-P4-006 is named by three FSD rows and carries no text anywhere.
read: RWB-AD-005 AC1 and Validation and messages; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 43 (rwb-access publishes AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged only); RWB-P4-E1022-APP section 14
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 2, 5, 7 (AC5, AC7), 8 (BR4, BR9), 12.3, 14 and 19; RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 4, 5, 8 and 12.3
confirm: security administrator role owner with the audit owner at the wave 4 design gate
impact: Gives the incident and the message an honest channel through the record that already exists and keeps a second event name and a new operation out of the estate; the business still has to fix the wording of MSG-P4-006

text: The session answer of GET /me/session (API-P4-012), declared by RWB-P4-E1037-CON, carries one field added by this key, conflictVersion, and that contract is named and never restated.
why: API-P4-012 states in its purpose that the session answers the matrix and conflict versions and declares no field name or field list, so the name and the shape of the conflict-version field are a decision, and the operation itself belongs to the permission-matrix contract of this service.
read: TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A.1 and T-A.2 API-P4-012; RWB-P4-E1037-CON (the session read and its schema); Ownership Map v1 (GET /me/session owned by P4)
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 3, 4, 7 (AC4), 8 (BR13) and 11; RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 1 and 4
confirm: session contract owner of RWB-P4-E1037-CON with the rwb-access tech lead
impact: One additive field within major version 1 and no second session operation; a rename before the freeze is free, and after it is a contract change

text: The two administrative reads of the separation-of-duty table sit on the /admin family of rwb-access with the Platform administration R letter of TSD P4 v3 T6.1, and the check itself declares no capability letter because it is called by the sign-in of the same service with a subject reference.
why: Neither read has an api row in the Ownership Map or in TSD P4 v3 appendix T-A, and the closest published administration operations of the same service, GET /admin/roles (API-P4-007) and GET /admin/access-log (API-P4-008), take Platform administration R, so the right is applied by analogy and the absence is carried.
read: TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (RW-SECADM CRUDA, RW-PLATADM CRUD, RW-AUDIT R in Platform administration), T-A.2 API-P4-007 and API-P4-008; FSD P4 v3 VR-P4-004-1; Ownership Map v1 api list
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 3, 7 (AC1, AC6), 8 (BR10), 12.1 and 15; RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 5, 10 and 12.1
confirm: security administrator role owner with the rwb-access service owner at the wave 4 design gate
impact: Keeps the pairs readable by the administration roles only and gives the check no letter, so a refusal can never be caused by a missing right of the person being refused

text: A refusal publishes no access event, and the load, the approval and the rollback of a new conflict version are the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON and not an operation of this contract; the access-policy event therefore belongs to that load path and not to this key.
why: The FSD requires a refusal event and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access no event for it, while slide 43 gives the service AccessPolicyChanged and DoaLimitChanged only, both of which are policy changes and neither of which a refusal is; no source gives the approval of a version of role_conflict an operation at all.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 43; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; RWB-P4-E1037-CON (the two loads of role, permission, masking_rule, role_conflict and delegation_limit and their approval); Ownership Map v1 ruling on the rule package registry (P7)
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 7 (AC5), 8 (BR4), 12.3, 13 and 19; RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 3, 4, 8 (BR12), 12.3 and 19
confirm: rwb-access contract owner with the permission-matrix contract owner of RWB-P4-E1037-CON
impact: One event name and one topic for the record, no invented access event, and the version lifecycle stays with the load path that already owns it

text: The separation-of-duty rule, its version and the refusal fact are delivered by this story's check on POST /api/recovery/access/v1/authorise/separation-of-duty, and the sign-in of RWB-P4-E1022-APP calls it after it resolves a person's role codes and before it answers a session; where that story's flow names a conflict check inside its resolver, the two are one call and the rule is written once.
why: The legacy criterion is observed at sign-in and the target keeps the session in the edge store, so the rule needs one home; the sign-in story owns the token, the second factor and the resolution, this story owns the pair table and the refusal, and the split has to be stated or the rule is built twice.
read: RWB-AD-005 Story and AC1; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 10, 14 and 41; RWB-P4-E1022-APP sections 4, 5 and 10; RWB-P4-E1022-CON (the authorise and me/permissions contract); Analysis of the sibling stories of the same service
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 1, 2, 4, 7 and 19; RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 1 and 4
confirm: rwb-access service owner with the sign-in story owner at the wave 4 design gate
impact: One rule and one refusal fact in the estate, called from one place; the sign-in keeps the session and this story keeps the rule, so neither story can silently duplicate the check

text: The conflict version in force is the version whose valid_from is the latest not after the date of the sign-in, one version answers whole, and a session keeps the conflict version it was checked against until it ends.
why: Legacy AC2 requires the next sign-in to be checked against a new version and the table carries valid_from and valid_to, while no source states how two rows of two versions are resolved on one date or what an open session keeps.
read: RWB-AD-005 AC2; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-209, DF-REF-210, DF-REF-211) and T3.2 (LOV-VERSION-STATUS); FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; RWB-P4-AD001-APP section 9 (the same version rule for the mapping)
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 4, 5, 8 (BR2, BR7) and 9; RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 7 (AC3), 8 (BR7) and 12.6
confirm: rwb-access service owner with the audit owner at the wave 4 design gate
impact: One version governs one sign-in and no person is refused by a version that started mid-day; the rule adds no column, because role_conflict already carries its version and dates

text: The environment code recorded on a refusal entry is read as a parameter through the parameters contract of rwb-case with the client library of DP-06, and it is never a constant, a profile value or a code literal.
why: The parameters contract is the estate's way to carry an environment value and this slice records the environment on the refusal entry, while no source names the parameter code that carries it.
read: Template and Rules §R5.5 (DP-06); RWB-PLT-E1042-CON and RWB-P3-E1042-CON; RWB-P4-AD001-APP section 13 (the same read for the mapping); Ownership Map v1 (parameter_catalog and parameter_value owned by P3)
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 1, 3, 5, 8 (BR11), 11 and 12.2; RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 3, 8 (BR11), 11 and 12.2
confirm: rwb-case parameters contract owner with the rwb-access service owner at the wave 4 design gate
impact: One build serves every environment and no environment code is written in code; the parameter code itself stays open until the parameters catalogue is frozen

text: A refused set refuses the whole session and is recorded as one local decision-record entry with decision code AC-DENY and reason code ROLE_CONFLICT in the same transaction, through the library of DP-03 whose dependency RWB-PLT-E1027-CON is carried by the app story and not by the contract.
why: The legacy criterion and the FSD refuse the session and require the refusal to be written, and no source states whether a refusal is partial or what it records; the decision-record library is the only writer of a refusal fact this service has.
read: RWB-AD-005 AC1; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03 and AC-EXC-P4-001-06; Template and Rules §R5.5 (DP-03); RWB-PLT-E1027-CON; Temporal and Drools Design Text Extract v1 (one transaction for state, record and outbox)
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 4, 5, 8 (BR3, BR5), 11 and 12.3; RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 3, 7 (AC3), 8 (BR9) and 12.3
confirm: rwb-access service owner with the audit owner at the wave 4 design gate
impact: No partial session survives a forbidden pair and every refusal is evidenced once; the dependency sits on the app story, so the contract story stays Day 1

text: The incident the criterion requires is the recorded refusal, whose addressee is the security administrator role RW-SECADM, and no incident queue, incident operation, target service or event name is created for it until an incident operation exists.
why: AC1 requires an incident to the security administrator and the FSD requires an incident to the security administrator queue, while no source names that queue, an operation or a target service, and Architecture v5 slide 14 gives rwb-access no event and no incident path.
read: RWB-AD-005 AC1; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 (P4 events: none) and slide 41 (P4 owns the access log); TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (RW-SECADM CRUDA in Platform administration)
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 1, 2, 4, 5, 8 (BR6), 14 and 19; RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 2, 8 (BR4) and 19
confirm: security administrator role owner with the platform architect at the wave 4 design gate
impact: The incident reaches the role that owns it through the record that already exists; a real incident operation later replaces the addressee and not the record

text: A new separation-of-duty version is loaded and approved through the load path of RWB-P4-E1037-CON, with the pairs travelling in the role matrix file of RWB-P4-E1019-APP, and the two rule-version paths of the legacy Endpoints table stay with P7 rwb-decision and the rule-version stories; this story's AC2 is answered from its own side by the check resolving the version in force at the next sign-in.
why: AC2 says the new version is approved, and neither the legacy story nor the FSD names the operation that approves a version of role_conflict; the legacy Endpoints table gives rule-version paths, which the Ownership Map ruling keeps with P7, so the approval has to be placed on a route that exists rather than invented here.
read: RWB-AD-005 AC2 and Endpoints; FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; Ownership Map v1 (rule_package registry owned by P7; role_conflict owned by P4); RWB-P4-E1037-CON (the two loads and their approval); RWB-P4-E1019-APP (the role matrix file and its conflict pairs)
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 3, 4, 7, 8 (BR12) and 19; RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 7 (AC5), 13 and 19
confirm: rwb-access service owner with the permission-matrix app owner and P7 rwb-decision at the wave 4 design gate
impact: A new pair reaches the next sign-in with no deployment and no new operation, and the approval keeps one route in the estate; if the business wants a dedicated approval it is a new contract and a new story

text: The text of MSG-P4-006 is fixed by no source, so this story fixes the message ID, the two role codes it names and the refusal it carries, writes no text of its own, and takes the text of RWB-P4-E1022-APP for the same ID only after the two agree before the freeze.
why: Three FSD exception rows name MSG-P4-006 and none of them gives its wording, the legacy message table holds five other IDs, and a sibling story of this run declares a text for the same ID, so writing a second text would give one condition two sentences.
read: FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03, AC-EXC-P4-002-03 and AC-EXC-P4-003-05; RWB-AD-005 Validation and messages; RWB-P4-E1022-APP section 14; RWB-P4-E1019-APP section 14 (the same ID left open)
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 1, 7, 8 (BR4), 13 and 14; RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 11 and 14
confirm: business owner of the access messages with the security administrator role owner at the wave 4 design gate
impact: One message ID and one sentence in the estate when the wording is fixed; until then a refused person sees the sentence the business chooses, and no test asserts a wording

text: A pair that forbids one role with any business role is carried as one role_conflict row per business role at the same conflict version, because conflicts_with holds one role code of varchar(30) and the schema has no wildcard and no second code list.
why: The FSD example states that RW-SECADM may not hold any business role, and TSD P4 v3 defines the pair as two single role codes, so the rule the specification describes cannot be stored as one row and its storage has to be decided.
read: FSD P4 v3 AC-EXC-P4-001-03; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (DF-REF-206 LOV-ROLE varchar(20), DF-REF-207 conflicts_with varchar(30)); TSD P4 v3 T6.1 (the business roles of the matrix); RWB-P4-E1019-APP (the role matrix file and its conflict pairs)
applied_in: RWB-P4-AD005-APP sections 1, 3, 8 (BR8), 11 and 13; RWB-P4-AD005-CON sections 7 (AC2) and 8 (BR6)
impact: The rule is storable without a schema change and the pair count grows with the business roles; a wildcard, if the business wants one, is a column change and a new version of the table
